The second most significant problem is bullying, with 55% of teens saying it is a major problem. Gangs and teen pregnancy are the least major problem, with just over 30% saying they were a major issue. This graph expresses that a vast majority of teens struggle with mental health, which is a problem that has been coming to greater attention in recent years. I wonder where these polls were taken, as interviewing teens in poorer areas would result in a greater response for issues like poverty and possibly gangs. One title for this graph could be "Major Problems for Teenagers."

raw_comment: Regarding this graph, I noticed that significant issues such as Anxiety & Depression, and Bullying are major worries for U.S. teenagers from ages 13-17. Here in Canada, teens would have similar concerns. As a 13 year-old, Drug addiction and Drinking alcohol are not concerns my age group, yet 50% of the people surveyed believed it was. I am curious as to why these two options are included in this graph because the age group surveyed are not legally allowed to drink or use these substances. I also wonder why Bullying isn't at the top of this graph because many of these issues can be contributed by bullying. Another thought I had was that some of these topics are vague, such as Anxiety, Depression, and Bullying, as they could be more specific. For example, Anxiety and Depression can be caused by the lack of socializing due to the overuse of social media and video games. Bullying can be separated into cyber, verbal, physical or racism because each has its own effects. I believe a catchy headline for this graph would be, "Bullying has Become a Major Teenage Problem." I think this is a good topic because in the past, while the other options were already big concerns, bullying wasn't recognized until a few years ago.
